solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pair shaken by 8's mascara running

indicators.note: mascara that is running has smudged out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mick Jagger's make-up streaks down his face as he performs.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is SIR MICK (Jagger), who shakes a pair of these on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Percussion rattles are played as a pair, one in each hand, and shaken to sound.

clue.text: Popular bar in ruins

definitions.meaning: a well-known chocolate bar sold in Britain and elsewhere
spoils or damages, as a verb

explanation.surface: A favourite pub lies in a state of dereliction.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the chocolate bar brand; the other is the verb meaning spoils or blemishes.

clue.text: 21 45 grow carrot

definitions.meaning: the 1963 debut single (a 45 rpm record) by the Rolling Stones
to progress or develop, as a crop or a pupil does
an inducement or lure held out to tempt someone

explanation.surface: Reads like a gardening note about the band's vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is STONES; a 45 is a seven-inch single, played at 45 rpm.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the Stones' first single, means to progress, and as a noun means an enticement.

clue.text: Don't move with new variety of tit in view

indicators.note: the shuffled bird is placed within the word for view

parts.note: a view is a sight

indicators.note: a new variety is a different form, so the bird's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher is told to keep still because a new kind of tit is visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new variety of' signals the anagram, and 'in' places it after the first two letters of the word for view.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay put and wait patiently is an idiom for refusing to move.

clue.text: One organising 21 had this in Oldham

definitions.text: One organising 21 had this in Oldham

parts.words: One organising 21 had this in Oldham
parts.note: Andrew Loog Oldham managed and promoted the early Rolling Stones, so the band had their showman-promoter in him

explanation.surface: Seems to say the band's organiser lived in the Lancashire town of Oldham.
explanation.walkthrough: Oldham is a town in Lancashire, but here it is Andrew Loog Oldham, the Stones' first manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A promoter or manager of entertainers is the theatrical term for the organiser of a show.

clue.text: Crossed the line, afraid right away, clutching 'Brideshead Revisited'

indicators.note: the shortened word for afraid holds the repeated letter within it
right is abbreviated R, and it is sent away from the word

parts.note: afraid means scared

indicators.note: visited again, so the letter is given a second time

parts.note: read as bride's head, its first letter B

explanation.surface: A frightened person nervously crosses a picket line while holding Waugh's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Brideshead' as bride's head, its first letter; 'Revisited' gives that letter a second time. Crossing a picket line is what a strikebreaker (a scab) does.
explanation.definitionFit: Working during a strike, crossing the picket line, is acting as a strikebreaker, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Neither up nor down, contrary Old Duke after a kiss? That's an absurd proposition

indicators.note: the reversed pair follows the A

parts.note: level, at par, neither above nor below the standard

indicators.note: contrary means turned the other way, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: X is the kiss written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer of a contrary old duke and a kiss calls the whole thing nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' turns OD into DO, placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-contradictory statement that seems absurd yet may hold true is the classic logical puzzle.

clue.text: Celebrant of golden anniversary today may be worried thus about taxman taking millions

indicators.note: the word for worried goes round the tax body and the millions

parts.note: one may be worried sick, so this is the word that completes the phrase
IR is the Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority

explanation.surface: A rock star might lie awake fretting over a big tax bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in 2012, the Rolling Stones' fiftieth year, so the celebrant is Mick Jagger, knighted in 2003.
explanation.definitionFit: The knighted Jagger was marking fifty years of the Rolling Stones when this puzzle appeared.

clue.text: Metal fan who upset 8's tasteful alter ego?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heavy-metal fan is annoyed by the singer's refined other persona.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'Sympathy for the Devil' Jagger sings 'I'm a man of wealth and taste', hence 'tasteful'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil narrating the Stones song introduces himself as a rich man of taste, a persona Jagger adopts.

clue.text: Original member of 21 getting 15 covered by Tina Turner

indicators.note: the rearranged singer's name wraps round the other piece
a turner turns things, so the name Tina is turned into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 15 is MUDDY WATERS, read as waters muddied, its letters stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A founding Stone records a song by an R&B hero that Tina Turner had covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is MUDDY WATERS, read as an instruction: its second word, muddied, is jumbled. 'Turner' jumbles the singer's name, which wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish pianist co-founded the Rolling Stones in 1962 and remained their road manager and keyboardist.

clue.text: Curry this third day being 21's creation

definitions.meaning: rhyming slang: a ... Murray (a 1950s singer) is a curry
add the third day of the week, counted from Sunday, and you have a Stones song title

explanation.surface: A curry on Tuesday is presented as the band's invention.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruby Murray was a 1950s Irish singer whose name is rhyming slang for curry; 'Ruby Tuesday' is a 1967 Stones hit.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is slang for a curry; the other completes the title of a famous Rolling Stones song.

clue.text: Cool jazz guitarist missing Juliet's dance

parts.note: to fan is to cool with a current of air

indicators.note: the guitarist's name lacks the letter for Juliet

parts.note: Django Reinhardt, the gypsy jazz guitarist
J is Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A trendy jazz guitarist sits out Juliet's dance at the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes J out of DJANGO to leave DANGO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Spanish dance for couples in triple time, often with castanets.

clue.text: Pet Shop Boys and Wham among others turn into clones

definitions.text: Pet Shop Boys and Wham among others
definitions.meaning: pop duos, pairs of performers working together
read cryptically, a performance (a turn) made twice over, copies of each other

explanation.surface: Pop duos are accused of becoming identical copies of each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Pet Shop Boys and Wham! were two-man British pop groups of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Pairs of performers billed together are duos; read literally, the phrase suggests turns that are duplicated.

clue.text: The truth goes out of the window embroiling party leader at length

indicators.note: the jumbled word draws the first letter of party into its midst
thrown out of the window, the word goes loses its order and is rearranged
a leader is at the front, so the first letter of party

explanation.surface: Truth is abandoned as a party leader gets entangled in a lengthy affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the window' rearranges GOES to GOSE, and 'embroiling' puts P inside to give GOSPE; L ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absolutely true is called this, after the Christian accounts treated as unquestionable.

clue.text: Dusty warmed up for 21 — an inspiration

indicators.note: stirred up, so the letters of these two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: Dusty Springfield warms up the crowd, inspiring the headline act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warmed' is part of the fodder, not the indicator: only 'up' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The blues singer's song 'Rollin' Stone' gave the band its name and his music shaped their sound.

clue.text: Dash for side of road where 8 lived

parts.note: to dash is to dart

indicators.note: a side here is an edge of the word, its final letter

explanation.surface: A pedestrian dashes for the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: Mick Jagger grew up in Dartford, a town in Kent just outside London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent town where Jagger was born and where he met Keith Richards at the station.

clue.text: Brand new interior for birthplace of 21 on 12 July 1962

parts.note: a marque is a make or brand, especially of car

indicators.note: the inside of the word new, its middle letter

explanation.surface: A newly branded venue claims to be where the band was born.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stones played their first gig at the Marquee Club in London's Soho on 12 July 1962.
explanation.definitionFit: The London jazz and rock club hosted the band's first ever performance on that date.

clue.text: The old pair of smalls you originally put on clean for return journey

indicators.note: the assembled string is sent back the other way, read right to left

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of the
S is the clothing abbreviation for small, twice

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of you

parts.note: to do the dishes is to clean them, so do means clean

explanation.surface: Someone packs fresh underwear for the trip home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smalls' is British slang for underwear, but here gives two S's; 'for return' reverses YESSYDO.
explanation.definitionFit: A long and eventful voyage, after Homer's epic about Odysseus's wandering trip home.

clue.text: One was one of 21 at 17; later, one was one of 21 in the park; rock royalty, almost!

definitions.text: One was one of 21 at 17; later, one was one of 21 in the park

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters are shaken into a new order
almost means not quite complete, so the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A trivia question about band members at different gigs and near-royal rockers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ROYALTY to ROYALT and 'rock' rearranges it. 17 is the Marquee Club; Hyde Park is the London park where the Stones played in 1969.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick played bass with the Stones at the Marquee debut, and Mick joined in time for the Hyde Park concert.

clue.text: Does a runner's muscle lose energy in moments?

parts.note: an ab is an abdominal muscle

indicators.note: the word for moments drops the letter for energy

parts.note: moments are seconds
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sprinter's muscles seem to fade within moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does a runner' is British slang for running off; 'lose' takes E from SECONDS to leave SCONDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee secretly, especially to avoid arrest or debt, is the slang 'do a runner'.

clue.text: With Ecstasy and no end of pot back on board ship there'll be a party tonight for this crew

definitions.text: there'll be a party tonight for this crew

indicators.note: on board a ship means inside its abbreviation

parts.note: SS is a steamship, as in prefixes to ship names

indicators.note: back means the short string is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written, a word giving its own letters

indicators.note: the end of pot is its last letter

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drugs on a party boat, with a celebration promised for the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for no plus the last letter of pot. The puzzle appeared on the Stones' fiftieth anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: The band celebrating its fiftieth birthday on the day the puzzle appeared is the crew in question.

clue.text: Liquid weedkiller missing standard tamper-proof top

indicators.note: the herbicide name loses both the norm and the initial letter

parts.note: paraquat is a herbicide
par is a standard or norm

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bottle of weedkiller lacks its childproof cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' strips PAR from the front and T from the end of PARAQUAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for water, used for liquids in pharmacy and chemistry.

clue.text: Obese and without a roof over one's head, ignoring inevitable conclusion is beyond comprehension

parts.note: obese means fat

indicators.note: ignoring means the word for roofless leaves out a letter

parts.words: without a roof over one's head
parts.note: having nowhere to live

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone overweight and sleeping rough finds life incomprehensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring inevitable conclusion' drops the E of inevitable from HOMELESS to leave HOMLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Too deep to be measured, and so figuratively impossible to understand.

clue.text: Vintage Tull out-take reviewed in 'Melody Maker'

indicators.note: reviewed means looked at again from the other end, read backwards
the letters are taken out of the words, found within them

explanation.surface: A music paper reviews an old unreleased Jethro Tull recording.
explanation.walkthrough: Melody Maker was a British weekly music paper; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument plucked to make tunes, so literally something that makes melody.

clue.text: 21 recording half this lament without original tune

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the wail goes round the other piece

parts.note: to cry is to lament

indicators.note: original suggests a new, inventive version, so the letters of tune are rearranged

explanation.surface: The band records a sad song lacking its first tune.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2012 the Stones had been recording for fifty years, half of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred years, so half of it is the fifty years the Stones had been making records.

clue.text: 21 rivals get the better of the French

parts.note: to beat is to get the better of
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: The band's rivals outdo the French.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liverpool group were the Stones' chief competitors in the 1960s British pop charts.
